title: Content patterns
goal: Show, with real components, how each KIND of content becomes a card or a row, and how one collection reads in three views — the reference an agent copies instead of inventing an arrangement.
primaryQuestion: How does this kind of content display here?
_why: A reference gallery in the product's own chrome: hub is the closest archetype (entries exist to be seen and copied, nothing is processed), and the screen deliberately shows the SAME collection three ways — which is exactly the case the view-switcher note in selection-rules governs: this collection is both visual (type tiles) and comparable (author, date), so the switcher is earned here and the rules' default (rows) loads first.

zones.name: collection
zones.answers: How does this kind of content display here?
zones.purpose: One collection, its DEFAULT view: rows in a flush panel — the representation these rules choose for this data (R4: browsing records reads as self-contained surfaces; ContentRow is the list answer). The SegmentedControl at the toolbar's trailing edge offers the two alternates, per the N-view-switcher note: this collection is both visual (the type tile identifies an item) and rich in fields worth columns, which is the only case the switcher is earned.

zones.name: alternate-views
zones.purpose: The SAME collection re-rendered on demand as cards (media wash carrying the glance) and as a table (all fields as columns) — the alternates the switcher offers. Task `read`, deliberately not a collection task and carrying no `data`: the collection is declared once in the zone above, and the rules judged it there; this zone exists because a reference screen for the switcher exception must show the exception. Every view truncates the same ordered field list (type, title, author, date, status).

zones.name: kinds
zones.purpose: The kind presets, one exhibit each, built only from registry parts: article (media top, eyebrow, excerpt), course (cover wash with the scrim carrying its own title), person (Identity, horizontal in lists and vertical only as the profile hero), file (a dense ContentRow), event (the date as the media block — the date IS the event's identity). Each exhibit is the composition an agent copies.

states.empty: Unreachable for the same reason; the deliberate absence of an EmptyState is recorded here so the validator's rule and this screen agree out loud.
states.error: No error state exists on purpose: nothing is fetched — a broken fixture fails the build, not the screen — so the deliberate absence of an Alert here IS the design, recorded so nobody adds one.

acceptance: The switcher changes representation, never data: the same items, the same order, in all three views.
Every view shows a prefix of the same ordered field list — no view invents a field another lacks entirely.
The course exhibit's title sits on the scrim, never on raw imagery or a raw wash.
The person exhibits show face-beside-name in the list form; vertical appears only in the profile-hero exhibit.
The switcher sits at the toolbar's trailing edge and the default view is the one the selection rules would choose (rows).
data: the collection: the showcase's MOCK_CONTENT (type, title, author, date, status) — real fixtures, no fetch
the kind exhibits: inline fixtures per kind, each naming its preset in the copy

behaviours.then: the collection renders as rows — the representation the selection rules choose for this data — with no table on screen
behaviours.why: The switcher offers alternates; the DEFAULT is never a preference, it is the rules' answer.

behaviours.when: the viewer switches to table and then to cards
behaviours.then: the same items appear in the same order in every view — the switch changes the reading, never the list
behaviours.why: The acceptance the research pinned: every view truncates one ordered field list.
